paragraphs.source_en: Third, authors of books on investing, are, in a real sense, captives of the eras that we have experienced. For example, when Benjamin Graham wrote *The Intelligent Investor* in 1949, he had *never* experienced a year in which the interest rate on bonds exceeded the dividend yield on stocks. By way of contrast, as I write this chapter in 2017, I have witnessed 60 consecutive years in which the dividend yield on stocks has *never* exceeded the interest rate on bonds. Turnabout, it seems, is fair play.
